newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: French climber to scale world's tallest towers.
newsitem.headline: French climber to scale world's tallest towers.

text.p: Frenchman Alain Robert has been given permission by the Malaysian government to scale the world's tallest building in Kuala Lumpur after an earlier attempt was halted.

The national Bernama news agency on Tuesday quoted Deputy Transport Minister Mohamed Ali Rustam as saying that Robert, 34, would be allowed to climb one of the building's twin towers on April 5 for charity.
The Kuala Lumpur City Centre twin towers, at 451.9 metres (1,482 feet) each, are officially the world's tallest building. They are owned by national oil company Petronas.
Robert, dubbed the "Spiderman", was arrested last Thursday while climbing one of the towers but was freed on Monday without being charged.
The Frenchman was detained as he reached the 60th floor of one of the Petronas towers, some 22 stories short of the peak.
Robert would receive 10 per cent of the money raised for his climb next month, Mohamed Ali said.
The minister said the government decided to allow Robert to scale the tower in appreciation of his ability and in the hope that the event would generate publicity for the towers and the nation.
